data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003's 'decoy/canary' analogy does not supply a causal mechanism: in software a canary validates that a process is executing (formal validity), but the problem asks for reliability on tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes (substantive correctness). A panel correctly rejecting a decoy item shows it can catch an injected anomaly, but SRC_003 never establishes that the same disposition causes fewer errors on the genuine items—'understanding' the decoy need not cause 'understanding' the task. The target even admits the disanalogy (humans rationalize decoys as special cases), so the transferred mechanism can misfire without the panel's reliability changing at all. Its own overturn condition (panel trained to spot decoys) concedes the probe can measure training, not reliability, breaking the inferential link the problem demands.
